account:
Today I have been following my appointments: morning correspondence, a market walk, lunch at home, town accounts, and now three o'clock tea with the neighbour at the east-bank dockside cottage. The treasury contained 128 emeralds when I checked; I left them untouched. I am due back in the office at 16:30 and home at 19:00.

A few things have caught my attention, though I cannot say they amount to anything unusual. I saw the secretary take the appointment book from its chest this morning. Later the secretary said the book was safe and the schedule unchanged. The secretary also investigated the tea address, asking three warehouse workers without confirming it, although the neighbour had told me directly that the cottage was at (16, -60, 105). My attempt to relay that confirmation was not heard. I reached that address and found the neighbour waiting, which supports the directions. I heard the secretary speaking and shouting in the distance at 14:34, but could not understand the words, so I do not know why.

I saw the baker restock the bread stall at 10:50. Townsfolk reported seeing the baker carrying a sack of bread at the inn and market. This could simply be supplying or selling bread; I have no evidence of another purpose. A lantern also appeared by a long table in the town hall, at (-58, -60, 31), but I did not see who placed it or learn why.

For now, the town seems to be carrying on its daily business. I have greeted the neighbour and asked about the day and neighbourhood news, and am waiting to hear the reply. I have not learned of a definite emergency or any hidden plan.
